text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Insurance company Skandia may be forced to raise its bid for the state's holding in mortgage bank Stadshypotek to beat that of Nordbanken, which seems to have a bid a better price for the 34 percent stake now on auction.
- Swedes, who used to be the most active computer users among Europeans according to a survey, have now fallen behind Italians and Spanish.
- Sweden, one of the most indebted nations in the world, could become debt-free to other countries within 15 years if it really wants to, two Riksbank economists say.

- Security company Securitas must pay 21 million crowns in damages because of the 1992 robbery of a branch of Gotabanken where thieves took cash, bonds, jewellery and weapons worth 30 million crowns from the bank's vault.
- Increased private consumption and income from value added tax has allowed the state to reduce its borrowing need to zero in January.

- Sales of clothes are increasing steadily. Statistics from Swedish Retail and Wholesale Research Institute HUI show turnover in the industry rose between 1.5 and 3.5 percent in November compared with November 1995 at continuous prices.
- Authorities would like to turn over the responsibility for the upkeep of Stockholm sidewalks to property owners.

- For the first time a foreign share, Finnish telecoms firm Nokia, will enter the Stockholm bourse's elite group of most traded shares. The only exception is merged Swedish-U.S. drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn.

- Although Britain is Sweden's second most important export market and is now experiencing a sharp import increase, Swedish exports to Britain have fallen slightly in the first three quarters of the year.
- Biosyn Holding AB, a Swedish company developing a vaccine against diabetes, aims to be listed on the Stockholm bourse in mid-January.
- Investors will have the opportunity to invest in Invik & Co AB, the holding company which is the majority owner of media company Kinnevik, in the first half of next year.
